findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow uses status: String plus lifecycle booleans (is_validated, is_sent). These fields can form illegal combinations independently: is_sent=true with status!="sent", both booleans true simultaneously, or status="sent" with is_sent=false. The compiler cannot enforce valid transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid state combinations silently persist, causing double-sends, missed validations, or incorrect audit logs depending on which field downstream code trusts.
findings.fix: Replace status + lifecycle booleans with a single enum typestate (e.g., LedgerStage::Created | Validated | Sent) with sent_at as a field only in the Sent variant. Remove is_validated and is_sent entirely.

findings.problem: pub status: String is used as a lifecycle indicator. String status fields are primitive-smell that allow arbitrary values and require repeated string comparison at every usage site.
findings.failure_mode: Typos, case mismatches, or unexpected string values silently break lifecycle checks throughout the codebase. String comparison is heap-allocated and slower than enum pattern matching.
findings.fix: Replace with a domain enum: pub status: LedgerStage, where LedgerStage is an enum of valid lifecycle states (Created, Validated, Sent). Pattern-match on the enum instead of comparing strings.

findings.problem: pub is_validated: bool is a lifecycle flag that should be part of a typestate enum. It is orthogonal to is_sent, enabling invalid combinations.
findings.failure_mode: A ledger can be validated after being sent, or sent without validation, depending on arbitrary ordering of boolean assignments. No invariant enforces the correct lifecycle order.
findings.fix: Fold is_validated into the typestate enum as an intermediate state (Validated) or a transition gate. The enum ensures only valid lifecycle progressions exist at the type level.

findings.problem: pub is_sent: bool is a lifecycle flag that should be part of a typestate enum. Combined with status: String and is_validated: bool, it enables O(n!) invalid state combinations.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code checking is_sent independently of status may process already-sent ledgers again, or skip processing ledgers where status="sent" but is_sent=false due to a bug.
findings.fix: Fold is_sent into the typestate enum as the terminal Sent state. The enum eliminates the boolean entirely and makes sent-at semantics explicit.

findings.problem: All fields of LedgerWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to set any combination of status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms arbitrarily without any invariant checks.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct or mutate LedgerWorkflow into an illegal state (e.g., is_sent=true, status="created"). This bypasses all lifecycle enforcement and turns the struct into a data bag with no domain semantics.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a smart constructor or builder that enforces lifecycle invariants. Use an enum typestate so the compiler prevents illegal states at the type level.

findings.problem: mark_sent directly mutates status and is_sent fields with string concatenation and boolean assignment, bypassing any type-level lifecycle enforcement. It has no preconditions, no error return for invalid transitions, and no validation of the source state.
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent can be called on a ledger in any state (including already-sent), causing double-sends, lost validation markers, or inconsistent sent_at timestamps. No railway error path exists for invalid transitions.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a state-machine transition function that takes the current state and returns Result<NewState, TransitionError>. Use enum-based states with explicit transitions (e.g., fn validate(LedgerStage::Created) -> LedgerStage::Validated). Marked sent should only accept the Validated state.

findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow has no constructor, newtype wrapper, or parse-boundary smart constructor. The id field is a raw String with no domain validation at construction time.
findings.failure_mode: Empty, malformed, or untrusted ledger IDs silently enter the system. Every caller must re-validate the id independently, violating the 'parse at boundaries' rule.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype LedgerId(String) with a fallible constructor LedgerId::new(s: &str) -> Result<LedgerId, ParseError> that validates format at the boundary. Replace pub id: String with pub id: LedgerId.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs mutable field assignment (an imperative action) on a struct with no functional core separation. There is no pure domain model or deterministic transition function — the logic is a bare mutation.
findings.failure_mode: No deterministic, testable core exists. The transition logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation from side effects, and the imperative mutation makes reasoning about state invariants impossible.
findings.fix: Define a pure transition function: fn mark_sent(stage: LedgerStage) -> Result<LedgerStage, TransitionError> that maps Validated -> Sent deterministically. Keep the struct as pure inert data with enum typestate.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no error return type. Invalid state transitions (e.g., marking a non-validated ledger as sent) cannot be represented as typed errors. No domain error enum exists.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid transitions either silently succeed (producing inconsistent state) or panic/unwrap in calling code. No caller can distinguish between 'already sent', 'not validated yet', and other failure modes.
findings.fix: Define a domain error enum: pub enum LedgerError { InvalidTransition { from: LedgerStage, to: LedgerStage }, AlreadySent }. Return Result<LedgerStage, LedgerError> from mark_sent.

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for mark_sent or any lifecycle transition. Performance claims (if any) cannot be verified.
findings.failure_mode: Unknown allocation behavior, cache performance, or branch prediction characteristics of the transition path. If mark_sent is called in hot paths, unmeasured String allocations on status field could be a bottleneck.
findings.fix: Add a microbenchmark for mark_sent comparing the current String-based approach against an enum-based typestate approach, measuring allocations and branch mispredictions.

findings.problem: No profiler data exists for the LedgerWorkflow lifecycle. String allocations on every mark_sent call are unprofiled.
findings.failure_mode: Hidden heap allocations from status: String and .to_string() in mark_sent may cause unnecessary GC pressure or cache misses in hot paths.
findings.fix: Run perf flamegraph or similar profiler on realistic workload to measure allocation frequency and latency of the current String-based status field.

findings.problem: mark_sent allocates a new String via "sent".to_string() on every call. No try_reserve or allocation-aware pattern is used because this is a small mutation, but the allocation is unbounded and repeated.
findings.failure_mode: Repeated heap allocations in hot paths degrade performance and increase memory fragmentation. In a high-throughput ledger system, this becomes a measurable bottleneck.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a non-allocating enum typestate. The enum discriminant is a single byte, eliminating all heap allocation on lifecycle transitions.

findings.problem: No second-ring evidence (tests, clippy, fmt) exists to verify the review findings. Static review alone cannot confirm whether downstream callers depend on the current field structure.
findings.failure_mode: The typestate refactoring may break existing callers that access .status, .is_validated, or .is_sent directly as pub fields. Without tests or command evidence, the scope of impact is unknown.
findings.fix: Run cargo check and cargo clippy after refactoring to enum typestate to surface all downstream field-access breakage. Add behavior tests covering valid and invalid state transitions.

missing_evidence: no benchmark for mark_sent or lifecycle transitions
no profiler data for allocation characteristics
no allocation tracking (try_reserve, Vec capacity patterns not applicable but String allocs unbounded)
no second-ring command evidence (cargo check/clippy/test) to verify refactoring scope
no behavior tests covering valid/invalid state transitions
residual_risk: Static review identifies fundamental typestate and encapsulation violations in LedgerWorkflow. The struct allows illegal state combinations through orthogonal String status and bool lifecycle flags. The mark_sent function bypasses all invariants. Without enum-based typestate, the domain model cannot enforce lifecycle correctness at compile time. The primary risk is silent state corruption leading to double-sends, missed validations, or incorrect audit trails. Enum typestate replacement and smart constructors are required to close these gaps.
